separateEqualAtRisk.name: Same-timestamp progression invocation order
facts: Both TS and PHP replay sort by at, then lexicographic command id. UUID randomness affects the tie order while replay remains deterministic for the same envelope.
Local UI creates Date.now timestamps before queued persistence; server discards client at and stamps its command while holding owner lock. Millisecond ties are possible in the data contract.

A reverse-lexical same-time buy/equip could replay equip first and reject; consecutive equips can choose UUID order rather than invocation order. No such timestamps/envelope were retained in this browser failure.
focusedProofRequired: Frozen timestamp and explicit reverse-lexical command IDs for buy then equip
Two owned equips at same timestamp in opposite input orders
TS/PHP canonical parity and previously stored-envelope replay
separateEqualAtRisk.migrationRequirement: Do not replace canonical tie sorting with insertion order casually. Any sequence or logical-clock change needs an explicit version/backward-compatibility plan preserving old stored results, idempotency and offline convergence.
